**David Michael Hasselhoff** (born July 17, 1952),[[1]] nicknamed "**the Hoff**",[[2]] is an American actor, singer, producer, and television personality. He first gained recognition on the soap opera _[The Young and the Restless]_ (1975–1982), playing the role of Dr. [Snapper Foster]. His career continued with his leading role as [Michael Knight] "Michael Knight (Knight Rider)") on the crime drama series _[Knight Rider] "Knight Rider (1982 TV series)")_ (1982–1986) and as L.A. County Lifeguard [Mitch Buchannon] in the drama series _[Baywatch]_ (1989–2000), the latter of which he also served as an executive producer.

Hasselhoff has appeared in films, including _[DodgeBall: A True Underdog Story]_ (2004), _[The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie]_ (2004), [_Click_] "Click (2006 film)") (2006), _[Hop] "Hop (film)")_ (2011), and _[Piranha 3DD]_ (2012). Before [Samuel L. Jackson], Hasselhoff was the first actor to portray the [Marvel Comics] character [Nick Fury] in the television film _[Nick Fury: Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D.] "Nick Fury: Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D. (film)")_ (1998). He made his [Broadway] debut in the musical _[Jekyll & Hyde] "Jekyll & Hyde (musical)")_ (2000) and went on to star in other musicals including _[Chicago] "Chicago (musical)")_ (2004) and _[The Producers] "The Producers (musical)")_ (2007).

Hasselhoff has released a total of [fifteen studio albums], which found success mostly in German-speaking parts of Europe, where he has garnered multiple gold and platinum awards, with the single "[Looking for Freedom] "Looking for Freedom (song)")" reaching number one in Germany and Switzerland. Hasselhoff has also worked as a talent show judge on television shows such as _[America's Got Talent]_ (2006–2009) and _[Britain's Got Talent]_ (2011).

## Early life and education

Hasselhoff was born in [Baltimore], Maryland, the son of Dolores Theresa (née Mullinex), a homemaker, and Joseph Vincent Hasselhoff, a business executive.[[1]][[3]] His family is [Roman Catholic] with German, English, and Irish descent.[[3]][[4]][[5]] His great-great-grandmother, Meta, emigrated with her family to Baltimore from [Völkersen], [Kingdom of Hanover], in 1865.[[6]]

He spent his childhood in [Jacksonville, Florida], and later lived in [Atlanta], Georgia, where he attended [Marist School] "Marist School (Georgia)"). Hasselhoff made his theatrical debut at the age of seven in _[Peter Pan] "Peter Pan (musical)")_, and ever since his childhood dream was to have a career on [Broadway] "Broadway (Manhattan)").[[7]] He graduated from [Lyons Township High School] in [La Grange, Illinois], in 1970.[[8]] He was a member of the speech team, senior discussion leaders, president of the choir, captain of the volleyball team and held roles in several plays (including one lead role as Matt in _[The Fantasticks]_). He studied at [Oakland University], then studied theater at the [California Institute of the Arts] until 1973.[[9]]
